original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In the formal three-register model over F2[AGL_2(F2)], can arbitrary free GL_3(F2) mixing reduce the six-call target diag([a],[b],[a*b*a*t_x]) to five calls when each paid label is restricted to a, b, or t_x?
scope_change_reason: After overlap review, the unrestricted affine rank theorem already settles the full rank-one affine-label alphabet. The experiment fixes the physically narrower three-label source alphabet and tests whether nonabelian dirty-register mixing exploits the remaining two-call gap above the rank relaxation.
bottleneck_link: A five-call identity would save one paid bit primitive in this explicit address-label model; the result is a scoped mechanism screen only and does not map to the selected rational-address supplier or change kappa.
stop_rule: Enumerate the complete formal matrix ball through radius three for the 84 paid generators, then test every canonical left prefix through radius two against the radius-three ball. Stop after all 4,782 joins; do not enlarge the alphabet or search radius.
evidence: The exact join found no target word of length at most five. The complete ball layer counts are 1, 84, 4,697, 232,720; all 4,782 left-prefix joins were checked. The direct six-call word replays exactly, so six is the minimum in this stated alphabet.
author: Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with scope refinement, verifier implementation, exact-search design, and package drafting. The author reviewed the model, charge accounting, code, and result.

open_questions.question: Can a different three-element affine rank-one label set over AGL_2(F2) produce a dirty-register compression for a mixed target triple?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This would distinguish a property of the chosen source labels from a broader obstruction to register-mixing savings.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the 3-label subsets of the nine affine rank-one elements and select target triples whose direct label-word bill exceeds the homogeneous-rank lower bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: This cycle fixed the source labels to a, b, and t_x; a wider catalogue search needs a separate seed, overlap check, and cost screen.
